analysis.title: Americas Retail: Specialty Hardlines: Promotional activity is mixed for 3Q26, with higher promotional breadth at Foot Locker sequentially
key_insights: Promotions in 3Q26 (8/3/26-10/29/26) were mixed y/y. In-store promotions were higher at Dick's and Academy than in comparable 3Q25, while online promotions were lower at both.
Dick's 3Q26 average in-store markdown activity was 7% with a 27% average promotion, vs 6% and a 34% average promotion in 3Q25. Online markdown activity was 18%, vs 27% in 3Q25.

Academy 3Q26 average in-store markdown activity was 25% with a 26% average promotion, vs 20% and 23% in 3Q25. Online markdown activity was 22%, vs 35% in 3Q25. Promotional breadth decreased sequentially in the second half of the quarter.

Foot Locker 3Q26 average in-store markdown activity was 28%, above the 24% historical average. The average promotion was 23%, below the 25% historical average. Breadth rose sequentially while depth fell sequentially.

GS reiterates Buy on DKS, citing health and wellness trends, brand heat, share gains, and gross margins and EBT well above pre-pandemic levels. The Foot Locker acquisition (closed 9/8/25) should strengthen vendor relationships.

GS does not think the more promotional industry changes Dick's competitive positioning or share capture, given its vendor relationships. It believes company guidance has been lowered enough to reflect these pressures.

GS reiterates Buy on ASO, citing expanded offerings, unit growth, and a valuation of 8.6x NTM P/E. Management says the slowdown in lifestyle footwear mainly hits mall-based chains and items outside Academy's assortment, and that there is no excess supply in the styles Academy carries.
Dick's management saw inventory build in parts of the industry during 2Q26, particularly in legacy footwear silhouettes and apparel franchises that are not resonating.

The 10/29/26 check showed in-store promotional breadth at Dick's up slightly from 10/19 and slightly above its historical average. Academy's breadth rose sequentially but stayed below its historical average. Online breadth rose at both but stayed below historical averages.

At Foot Locker, promotional breadth in 3Q26 has trended above historical levels, likely because of elevated industry inventory. Overall depth is still below historical levels but has trended above in October.

Foot Locker channel check (Union Square, 10/29/26): light traffic, healthy in-stocks, and a Kids clearance table with a 2 for $99 promotion. Timberland replaced Salomon as the first footwear display, and Nike was moved to the end of the Women's assortment.
Foot Locker is more promotional in store (29% of footwear selection on promotion) than online (21%). Online breadth rose vs the 10/19 check.
Dick's announced 124 new footwear releases for Oct'26 vs 79 in Sept'26. Foot Locker announced 83 vs 80. Nike is 55.6% of Dick's October releases and 50.6% of Foot Locker's.
Golf Galaxy in-store promotion averaged 29% of each section in October vs 23% in September, with golf apparel at about 45%. Online, Dick's golf promotion averaged 18% in October, below 36% in Oct'25.

market_movers.rationale: Health and wellness trend, brand heat, share gains and structurally higher margins. Guidance is seen as sufficiently lowered for promotional pressure.
Expanded offerings, emerging unit growth story, and valuation at 8.6x NTM P/E.

sector_views.rationale: The industry has become more promotional on elevated footwear and apparel inventory, but the backdrop is described as strong and promotions are mixed y/y.

earnings_insights: DKS 3Q26 (8/3/26-10/29/26) promotional tracking, not reported earnings: average in-store markdown activity 7% vs 6% in 3Q25.
GS believes DKS guidance, which was lowered at 2Q earnings on 8/25/26, now reflects industry promotional pressure.
GS sets the DKS price target at $170, from relative P/E multiples of 40%/45%/50% (downside/base/upside), and the ASO target at $63, from 35%/40%/45%.
risk_factors: DKS: weaker demand amid economic uncertainty, delays in improving the Foot Locker business, inventory overhang and discounting in the industry, DTC initiatives from major brands, and weaker sports participation.

ASO: Nike could limit product distribution to ASO, weaker omnichannel and digital capabilities vs competitors, and a possible pullback in consumer demand if pandemic-era sporting goods demand proves to be pull-forward.

tension_points.bull_case: GS says a strong industry backdrop, vendor relationships and access to innovative designs let Dick's keep its competitive position and share gains. It believes guidance already reflects the pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated industry footwear and apparel inventory is raising promotional breadth, especially at Foot Locker. Legacy silhouettes are not resonating and in-store promotions are higher y/y at Dick's and Academy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further inventory overhang and discounting in the industry, or delays in improving the Foot Locker business.

theme_stances.key_argument: Industry promotions are mixed y/y, but GS does not think they change Dick's competitive positioning.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not believe this changes Dick’s competitive positioning

theme_stances.key_argument: Promotional breadth at Foot Locker has started to trend above historical levels, likely due to elevated industry inventory.
theme_stances.evidence: promotional breadth has started to trend above historical levels
